body.title: Security review extension points for the review framework
body.intent: Extend the rebuilt review framework (ReviewContext, abstract Feedback, controller-configured severity, extensible Locator/Pointer, per-review-type checkpoint/validator, Scope, reconciliation pass, docgen 'review-report') to satisfy the security-quality-review PRD, without reshaping the already-converged abstractions. ONE new 'security' review type hosts all of the PRD's deterministic capabilities. These capabilities (risk-family selection, secret-scan, SAST, SBOM/dependency, IaC/container, language-native checks, security-graph build, policy evaluation, sandbox verification/mutation) are DELEGATES — named steerings the security reviewer is aware of and selects ONE AT A TIME, sequentially, gated by risk-family applicability (not-applicable skips with a recorded reason; applicable/uncertain run, uncertain cautiously) — entirely internal to the security validator's own control flow, with the generic checkpoint/validator contract left untouched. Within one review round the sequence is: primary reviewer pass -> security reviewer pass -> reconciliation (reconciliation runs only on round > 1, unchanged from the already-converged process). Security is further sub-typed by concern (data / endpoint / vulnerability), and its own scope additionally covers newly added dependencies, newly exposed services, and new/changed data access. Findings are modeled via TRUE INHERITANCE, not wrapping-by-reference: Feedback (abstract base) -> SecurityFinding (concrete subclass carrying check-ID, policy reference, evidence, fixability, a `confidence` field for uncertain-family output, and an orthogonal policy `enforcementMode` of advisory/warning/blocking) -> further subclassed per security subtype or per risk family as needed. Because SecurityFinding IS-A Feedback, it participates in the shared cross-reviewer reconciliation pass and in the docgen 'review-report' renderer via ordinary polymorphism — there is no unwrap/rehydration step and no id-matching reconciliation boundary; the renderer simply type-discriminates to render SecurityFinding's extra fields in a dedicated section, and review-report stays one unified doc type. A 'blocking' enforcementMode rides the framework's existing severity-driven block/approval gate (no new gate type). Policy overrides are simple overriddenBy/overrideReason/overriddenAt fields directly on SecurityFinding (no separate back-referencing override record), anchored to a code revision: the override lapses once the scope's current revision diverges, forcing re-evaluation. Risk-family verdicts (applicable/not-applicable/uncertain + reason), including not-applicable ones that produce no true finding, are themselves represented using the same SecurityFinding hierarchy as informational, zero-severity records for durable audit visibility — not a separate parallel type. Primary-finding dedup across SecurityFindings (the same vulnerability surfaced by multiple checkpoints collapsing to one primary finding with corroborating evidence) runs as a step scoped entirely inside the security validator, after its own checkpoints and before handoff to the framework's shared reconciliation pass, which is otherwise untouched. Security-graph and evidence-provider code-location citations use a new SecurityLocator type that extends Locator/Pointer with first-class security fields (trust-boundary id, taint-path step index) -- the same open-Locator-kind extensibility pattern already established. The five evidence-provider categories are invoked through a new dedicated EvidenceProvider interface/registry, distinct from the general ~110-entry tool registry but still routed through daemon IPC (staying within the tool boundary), with a common input/output contract feeding SecurityFinding.evidence uniformly. The sandbox-verification/mutation-testing checkpoint produces a distinct VerificationReceipt type -- which should inherit/extend the framework's existing feedback-completion/test-record pattern rather than being designed as an unrelated concept -- independent of SecurityFinding, recorded for every run (pass or fail) regardless of outcome, persisted in a durable per-review-round record file (e.g. RECEIPTS.md) beside the review artifact, mirroring the existing TESTS.md-beside-BUILD.md convention; a corroborated SecurityFinding references the receipt by id. Two significant items are deliberately PARKED rather than resolved here, each deserving its own dedicated future session: (1) governed learnings (human-approved corrections durably improving future reviews) -- relevance-scoping human feedback is a hard problem in its own right, not just a placement decision; (2) actually building and persisting the security/vulnerability graph (trust boundaries, sources, sanitizers, sinks, interprocedural source-to-sink paths) -- this is indexer-level work (tree-sitter parsing, entity/relation construction, incremental reindexing) and not a simple data-structure choice; the transient-in-memory choice recorded in this session's decision list is a non-committal placeholder only, not a real decision. Finally, a cross-cutting rule applies to ALL of this session's and the prior two sessions' union/inheritance-heavy data model (Feedback/SecurityFinding, Locator/SecurityLocator, Scope's scopeType/scopeLevel, VerificationReceipt, etc.): the canonical model keeps real inheritance/discriminated unions as designed for humans, but the JSON Schema actually presented to a given LLM/provider for structured output must be TUNED per (type, target model) pair via dedicated bidirectional transformers (input-side: canonical model -> a shape that model reliably emits against; output-side: parsing its response back into the canonical model) -- extending the pattern already used for the codex provider -- rather than committing to one universal encoding style (e.g. a single flat-discriminated-union rule) for every type and model.
body.scopeBoundary: This spec converges the EXTENSION POINTS and BOUNDARIES for plugging the security-quality-review PRD into the already-converged review framework -- which abstractions the PRD's new concerns reuse unchanged (Feedback via subclassing, Locator via subclassing, the checkpoint/validator contract, the reconciliation pass, the docgen review-report doc type, the existing severity-driven gate) and which genuinely need new structure (SecurityFinding, SecurityLocator, EvidenceProvider registry, VerificationReceipt, the security review type's internal delegate/checkpoint control flow). It does not design the full internals of risk-family taxonomy, evidence-provider implementations, the security graph schema, a policy-as-code DSL, or the mutation-testing harness; it does not cover all 37 FRs or the PRD's 7-phase rollout sequencing; and it deliberately defers governed learnings and security-graph construction/persistence to their own dedicated future brainstorming sessions rather than deciding them now.
nonGoals: Full design of risk-family taxonomy, evidence-provider internals, security graph schema, policy-as-code DSL, or mutation-testing harness internals in this session
Full design of the governed-learnings approval UX in this session; deferred entirely including structural placement
Re-litigating the already-converged Feedback/Locator/Scope/checkpoint/reconciliation model from prior brainstorm sessions
Covering all 37 FRs or the 7-phase rollout sequencing in this sitting
Designing a separate pipeline/stage outside the existing round-based review process for evidence-gathering work
A second new review type alongside 'security'
Extending the base Feedback type itself to carry check-ID/policy/evidence/fixability fields
Running primary-finding dedup for SecurityFindings through the framework's shared cross-reviewer reconciliation pass
Full design of change-risk summaries / deep repository scan triggers and scheduling in this session
Introducing a new policy-specific gate type separate from the existing severity-driven block mechanism
Persisting the security graph as a standalone structure in the daemon's LMDB graph store or a separate dedicated store
Invoking evidence providers as ad-hoc direct calls with no new abstraction, or as plain entries in the general tool registry
Making SecurityFinding itself a Feedback subtype
Modifying the shared reconciliation pass's type signature or logic to understand SecurityFinding directly, or threading SecurityFinding-specific fields through it
Modifying the generic per-review-type checkpoint/validator contract to add built-in ordering/skip-if-prior-verdict semantics for any review type
Redesigning docgen's review-report layout/visual style beyond adding a rendering path for SecurityFinding's extra fields
B — Multiple new review types, one per capability family (evidence-scan, security-graph, policy-gate, verification), each with its own checkpoint/validator inside the existing round structure

C — New pre-review evidence pipeline (outside the round process) that runs providers/graph/policy once per Scope and produces an evidence bundle; a single 'security' review type consumes that bundle during rounds via existing Locator/severity to emit Feedback
D — Evidence gathering is not a review-framework concern at all; it runs as a separate daemon capability whose output is handed to reviewers as ordinary context, with no new review type
B — Phase-level: a small number of coarser checkpoints (e.g. 'evidence-gathering', 'graph-and-policy', 'verification') that each internally orchestrate several PRD capabilities
C — Monolithic: a single 'security-evidence' checkpoint that runs the entire pipeline internally and only reports final SecurityFindings
A — Enforcement mode IS severity: map policy config directly onto the existing severity scale, one field, no new axis

C — Enforcement mode lives only in the policy-evaluation checkpoint's own output, not on SecurityFinding at all; severity is set once via a static policy-to-severity mapping table checked in per-repo config

A — Reuse the existing reconciliation pass: SecurityFinding dedup is just the reconciliation pass's merge logic operating on SecurityFindings like any other Feedback, keyed by (check-ID, Locator) instead of/alongside whatever key it already uses

C — No dedup at this layer at all: checkpoints emit SecurityFindings independently and primary/corroborating identity is left as a downstream (e.g. docgen 'review-report' rendering) concern, not a review-time concept
B — Always-run: every evidence checkpoint executes regardless of risk-selection; the risk-selection verdict is attached to findings as advisory context only, never gates execution

C — Partial gating: risk-selection only gates the expensive/slow checkpoints (sandbox verification/mutation testing); the cheap deterministic scanners (secret-scan, SAST, SBOM, IaC, language-native) always run regardless of the verdict

A — Reuse the existing extensible Locator/Pointer as-is; security-graph-specific context (trust-boundary id, taint-path step index, provider/tool name, rule id) rides alongside as an opaque metadata bag on the evidence entry, not inside Locator itself
C — Fully separate evidence-reference structure independent of Locator (e.g. internal graph node IDs resolved only within the security review type)

A — Governed learnings are a new internal checkpoint/state of the 'security' review type's validator: corrections are captured, human-approved, and fed back to tune that review type's own risk-selection/evidence-provider/policy checkpoints on later runs. No new framework-level structure.

B — Governed learnings are a new framework-level mechanism (a learnings store + approval gate sitting alongside, not inside, review types), since corrections are really about reviewer-process quality and could apply to any review type, not just security.
A — Receipt lives only as evidence inside a SecurityFinding: no separate receipt type; if verification found nothing, no record persists beyond the checkpoint's own pass/fail status

C — Fold receipts into the checkpoint's own stage-report record (the existing per-checkpoint validator output already written for every checkpoint), with no new type at all — just require the sandbox/mutation checkpoint's stage-report to carry the isolation/outcome detail

A — New override record (revision + check-ID/policy-ref keyed), consulted by the policy-evaluation checkpoint before it stamps enforcementMode; SecurityFinding only ever carries the final effective mode, override is separate durable data the checkpoint reads
C — Route overrides through the framework's shared reconciliation pass as a generic cross-review-type override mechanism, reusable beyond security findings

B — Separate policy gate: the policy-evaluation checkpoint independently fails/blocks the round when it finds a 'blocking' verdict, regardless of the finding's severity — a second, parallel block path alongside the severity-driven one

C — Metadata only: enforcementMode never blocks the round directly; it is surfaced as an annotation in the report, and anything that should actually block must also be given a correspondingly high severity by the reviewer
B — Encode confidence by capping enforcementMode (e.g. uncertain-family findings can never exceed 'advisory')
C — Confidence lives only on the risk-family verdict (checkpoint-level artifact), not copied onto each SecurityFinding

A — New RiskFamilyVerdict type: one durable record per family per security review run (family id, verdict, reason, confidence), stored alongside SecurityFindings and VerificationReceipts regardless of whether the family produced any finding

B — No new type: the risk-selection checkpoint's per-family verdicts live only as that checkpoint's own skip/pass metadata inside the existing per-checkpoint validator mechanism, with no separate durable record
A — Persist as new entity/relation kinds in the existing LMDB graph store, reusing the core traversal API
C — Separate dedicated store (e.g. an artifact file alongside the review record) independent of both the core graph API and inline finding evidence

A — New tool-registry entries: each provider becomes a new built-in tool wrapper (like the existing ~110 git/shell/http/etc. tools), invoked by checkpoints through the same general daemon tool-call mechanism as everything else
C — Ad-hoc: checkpoint code calls external scanners/binaries directly via the existing shell/exec tool, with no new provider abstraction or registry at all
A — New LMDB entity/relation kind in the daemon's existing graph store, queryable via the typed graph API alongside other entities
C — Embedded inline within the security review type's own artifact/output only, with no separate record file or store
D — A new dedicated store/table outside both the graph and artifact files (a separate persistence layer just for receipts)
B — Anchored to the review round/artifact only: the override stays valid until a human explicitly revokes it, with no automatic lapsing tied to subsequent code changes

C — Explicit validity window set by the approver: add a validUntilRevision (or similar) field the approver fills in at override time, checked against the scope's current revision each round; absent a value it behaves like B
A — Extend Feedback itself with optional fields (checkId, violatedPolicyRef, evidence[], fixability) that only the 'security' review type populates
C — Put the extra fields in Feedback's existing extensible metadata/details bag instead of named fields

Generalize reconciliation to a minimal structural interface (severity + locator/pointer + reviewer id) that both Feedback and SecurityFinding satisfy, so SecurityFinding flows through reconciliation directly as itself via delegation

Record reconciliation's outcome as a new status field directly on the wrapped Feedback inside SecurityFinding (no separate rehydration pass); the SecurityFinding object is mutated in place during reconciliation via a reference held by the security validator
A — Generic framework capability: extend the checkpoint/validator contract itself with ordering + skip-if-prior-verdict metadata, available to any review type
C — Hybrid: generic contract gains an optional per-checkpoint 'skipped' result value, but the decision of which checkpoints to run/skip remains internal to each review type's validator

B — Keep review-report strictly Feedback-only and oblivious to SecurityFinding; the security review type emits its own separate rendering (e.g. a companion section or file) for the extra fields, outside the shared docgen path
C — Add a new docgen docType (e.g. 'security-report'), generated only when a security review type ran, fully separate from 'review-report'
A non-IS-A wrapper object that holds a reference to a separately embedded base Feedback instance, rather than a true subclass

An unwrap-rewrap handoff step: pass each surviving primary SecurityFinding's wrapped base Feedback into reconciliation untouched, then match the outcome back by id onto the originating SecurityFinding afterward (superseded — there is no wrapped Feedback to unwrap)

Security is further sub-typed by concern (data / endpoint / vulnerability), and its own scope additionally covers newly added dependencies, newly exposed services, and new/changed data access. Within one round the sequence is: primary reviewer pass -> security reviewer pass -> reconciliation (reconciliation only on round > 1, unchanged from the already-converged process)
ruledOut: B — Multiple new review types, one per capability family (evidence-scan, security-graph, policy-gate, verification), each with its own checkpoint/validator inside the existing round structure

C — New pre-review evidence pipeline (outside the round process) that runs providers/graph/policy once per Scope and produces an evidence bundle; a single 'security' review type consumes that bundle during rounds via existing Locator/severity to emit Feedback

decisions.reason: Where does the PRD's deterministic evidence-gathering work (risk-family selection, evidence providers, security graph construction, policy-as-code evaluation) sit relative to the existing round-based review process?

decisions.chosen: A — Fine-grained: one checkpoint per capability (risk-selection, secret-scan, SAST, SBOM/dependency, IaC/container, language-native checks, security-graph build, policy evaluation, sandbox verification/mutation) — each independently gated and reported through the existing per-checkpoint validator mechanism
ruledOut: B — Phase-level: a small number of coarser checkpoints (e.g. 'evidence-gathering', 'graph-and-policy', 'verification') that each internally orchestrate several PRD capabilities
C — Monolithic: a single 'security-evidence' checkpoint that runs the entire pipeline internally and only reports final SecurityFindings
decisions.reason: The PRD's evidence-gathering work (risk-family selection, per-category evidence providers, security-graph construction, policy-as-code evaluation, sandbox verification/mutation) runs inside the 'security' review type's validator as checkpoint stages. What granularity should those checkpoints have?

decisions.chosen: B — Orthogonal: SecurityFinding carries both severity (the reviewer/controller's assessment, unchanged contract) and a separate policy enforcementMode field (advisory/warning/blocking) derived from policy-as-code at evaluation time
ruledOut: A — Enforcement mode IS severity: map policy config directly onto the existing severity scale, one field, no new axis

C — Enforcement mode lives only in the policy-evaluation checkpoint's own output, not on SecurityFinding at all; severity is set once via a static policy-to-severity mapping table checked in per-repo config
decisions.reason: The PRD's policy-as-code gate has its own advisory/warning/blocking enforcement modes (with revision-bound overrides), separate from the existing review framework's controller-configured severity scale that every Feedback already carries. How should a policy violation's enforcement mode relate to the SecurityFinding's severity?

decisions.chosen: B — Separate dedup step inside the 'security' review type's validator, run after its own checkpoints but before the framework's reconciliation pass hands off: SecurityFinding-specific primary/corroborating linkage is fully internal to the security review type
ruledOut: A — Reuse the existing reconciliation pass: SecurityFinding dedup is just the reconciliation pass's merge logic operating on SecurityFindings like any other Feedback, keyed by (check-ID, Locator) instead of/alongside whatever key it already uses

C — No dedup at this layer at all: checkpoints emit SecurityFindings independently and primary/corroborating identity is left as a downstream (e.g. docgen 'review-report' rendering) concern, not a review-time concept
decisions.reason: The PRD wants a dedup'd 'primary finding' identity across SecurityFindings (e.g. the same vulnerability surfaced by SAST, the security graph, and a policy rule should collapse to one primary finding with the others as corroborating evidence). The existing framework already has a dedicated reconciliation pass that runs after all review-type checkpoints to merge/reconcile Feedback across reviewers. Should primary-finding dedup for SecurityFindings reuse that existing reconciliation pass, or run as a separate step scoped to the security review type?

decisions.chosen: A — Gating: a family marked not-applicable skips its corresponding checkpoint(s) entirely, recorded as skipped-with-reason; applicable and uncertain families run their checkpoints (uncertain runs cautiously, e.g. flags low-confidence results)
ruledOut: B — Always-run: every evidence checkpoint executes regardless of risk-selection; the risk-selection verdict is attached to findings as advisory context only, never gates execution

C — Partial gating: risk-selection only gates the expensive/slow checkpoints (sandbox verification/mutation testing); the cheap deterministic scanners (secret-scan, SAST, SBOM, IaC, language-native) always run regardless of the verdict
decisions.reason: The PRD's first checkpoint is context-sensitive risk-family selection, which judges each risk family applicable / not-applicable / uncertain with reasons. Does that verdict control whether the 'security' review type's later evidence checkpoints (secret-scan, SAST, SBOM, IaC/container, language-native checks, security-graph build, policy evaluation, sandbox/mutation) actually run for this scope, or do all checkpoints always run regardless of the risk-selection outcome?

decisions.chosen: B — New SecurityLocator type that extends Locator with first-class security fields (trust-boundary id, taint-path step index)
ruledOut: A — Reuse the existing extensible Locator/Pointer as-is; security-graph-specific context (trust-boundary id, taint-path step index, provider/tool name, rule id) rides alongside as an opaque metadata bag on the evidence entry, not inside Locator itself
C — Fully separate evidence-reference structure independent of Locator (e.g. internal graph node IDs resolved only within the security review type)
decisions.reason: The security graph (trust boundaries, sources, sanitizers, sinks, source-to-sink paths) and other evidence-provider output must cite code locations inside a SecurityFinding's evidence field. Should these citations reuse the existing extensible Locator/Pointer abstraction, a new security-specific Locator subtype, or a separate evidence-reference structure decoupled from Locator entirely?

decisions.chosen: C — Defer the placement decision entirely: treat governed learnings as fully out of scope for this brainstorm (not just its UX), to be boundary-decided in a later session once the security review type ships.
ruledOut: A — Governed learnings are a new internal checkpoint/state of the 'security' review type's validator: corrections are captured, human-approved, and fed back to tune that review type's own risk-selection/evidence-provider/policy checkpoints on later runs. No new framework-level structure.

B — Governed learnings are a new framework-level mechanism (a learnings store + approval gate sitting alongside, not inside, review types), since corrections are really about reviewer-process quality and could apply to any review type, not just security.
decisions.reason: The PRD wants human-approved 'governed learnings' from reviewer corrections (e.g. a human overturns a SecurityFinding — wrong risk-family call, false-positive evidence, bad policy match — and that correction should durably improve future reviews). Where does this governed-learnings mechanism structurally plug into the framework: inside the 'security' review type itself, or as a framework-level mechanism outside any single review type?

decisions.chosen: B — New VerificationReceipt type, independent of SecurityFinding, recorded by the sandbox/mutation checkpoint for every run (pass or fail); a SecurityFinding that verification corroborates references the receipt by id, but the receipt persists on its own. VerificationReceipt should inherit/extend the framework's existing feedback-completion/test-record pattern rather than being designed as an unrelated concept

decisions.reason: The sandbox-verification/mutation-testing checkpoint must produce durable receipts (what ran, in what isolated environment, with what outcome) that persist even when no finding results. Where does a verification receipt structurally live relative to SecurityFinding and the review framework's existing records?

decisions.chosen: B — Override lives as fields on SecurityFinding itself (overriddenBy/overrideReason/overriddenAt), finding keeps its originally-computed blocking mode and the override is a visible annotation on top
ruledOut: A — New override record (revision + check-ID/policy-ref keyed), consulted by the policy-evaluation checkpoint before it stamps enforcementMode; SecurityFinding only ever carries the final effective mode, override is separate durable data the checkpoint reads
C — Route overrides through the framework's shared reconciliation pass as a generic cross-review-type override mechanism, reusable beyond security findings
decisions.reason: The PRD's policy-as-code gate needs revision-bound overrides for a blocking enforcement verdict (e.g. a reviewer/owner exempts a specific finding at a specific revision from blocking). Given enforcementMode is already orthogonal to severity (decision 4) and policy-specific logic already stays inside the security validator rather than the shared reconciliation pass (decision 5), where should the override itself structurally live relative to SecurityFinding and the policy-evaluation checkpoint?

decisions.chosen: A — Reuse existing gate: a 'blocking' enforcementMode finding is reported through the same mechanism a HIGH/MED severity finding already uses to block the review round/approval — no new gate type, policy violations ride the existing severity-driven block path
ruledOut: B — Separate policy gate: the policy-evaluation checkpoint independently fails/blocks the round when it finds a 'blocking' verdict, regardless of the finding's severity — a second, parallel block path alongside the severity-driven one

C — Metadata only: enforcementMode never blocks the round directly; it is surfaced as an annotation in the report, and anything that should actually block must also be given a correspondingly high severity by the reviewer
decisions.reason: A SecurityFinding's policy enforcementMode can be 'blocking' (decision 4: orthogonal to severity). How should a 'blocking' verdict interact with the existing review framework's own round pass/block outcome and approval gate?

decisions.chosen: A — New `confidence` field directly on SecurityFinding (e.g. high/medium/low), independent of severity and enforcementMode
ruledOut: B — Encode confidence by capping enforcementMode (e.g. uncertain-family findings can never exceed 'advisory')

decisions.chosen: CORRECTED: SecurityFinding is a concrete SUBCLASS of the abstract Feedback base (true inheritance, IS-A), not a wrapper object holding a reference to an embedded Feedback instance — `Feedback` (abstract) -> `SecurityFinding`/`SecurityFeedback` (concrete, carrying check-ID, violatedPolicyRef, evidence[], fixability, confidence, enforcementMode), further subclassable per security subtype (data/endpoint/vulnerability) or per risk family as needed

Does this richer shape extend the existing abstract Feedback type directly, or sit as a separate SecurityFinding wrapper that references a Feedback?

ruledOut: Generalize reconciliation to a minimal structural interface (severity + locator/pointer + reviewer id) that both Feedback and SecurityFinding satisfy, so SecurityFinding flows through reconciliation directly as itself via delegation (unnecessary once SecurityFinding IS-A Feedback)

Record reconciliation's outcome as a new status field directly on the wrapped Feedback inside SecurityFinding (no separate rehydration pass); the SecurityFinding object is mutated in place during reconciliation via a reference held by the security validator (unnecessary once SecurityFinding IS-A Feedback)

An unwrap-rewrap handoff step: pass each surviving primary SecurityFinding's wrapped base Feedback into reconciliation untouched, then match the outcome back by id onto the originating SecurityFinding afterward (superseded — there is no wrapped Feedback to unwrap)
decisions.reason: Decision 17 (as originally drafted) made SecurityFinding wrap a base Feedback rather than extend it, raising the question of how a deduped SecurityFinding gets processed by the framework's shared cross-reviewer reconciliation pass, which is typed to operate on Feedback instances. With the inheritance correction, this question dissolves: no unwrap/rewrap mechanism is needed at all.

decisions.chosen: B — Entirely internal: the security validator's own code decides which checkpoints to run/skip based on risk-family verdicts, and only reports the ones it runs through the existing generic checkpoint-report API unchanged
ruledOut: A — Generic framework capability: extend the checkpoint/validator contract itself with ordering + skip-if-prior-verdict metadata, available to any review type
C — Hybrid: generic contract gains an optional per-checkpoint 'skipped' result value, but the decision of which checkpoints to run/skip remains internal to each review type's validator
decisions.reason: Decision 5 established that risk-family verdicts gate which later security checkpoints run (not-applicable skips, applicable/uncertain run). Does that gating require a new generic capability added to the framework's already-converged per-review-type checkpoint/validator contract (ordering + skip-if-prior-verdict metadata, usable by any review type), or does it stay entirely internal to the security review type's own validator function, with the generic contract untouched?

decisions.chosen: A — Extend the review-report renderer to detect a SecurityFinding-typed record (via a type discriminant on the SAME Feedback instance reconciliation already operated on — not a separate unwrapped copy) and render its extra fields in a dedicated section per finding; review-report stays one unified doc type with conditional rendering
ruledOut: B — Keep review-report strictly Feedback-only and oblivious to SecurityFinding; the security review type emits its own separate rendering (e.g. a companion section or file) for the extra fields, outside the shared docgen path
C — Add a new docgen docType (e.g. 'security-report'), generated only when a security review type ran, fully separate from 'review-report'
decisions.reason: The existing docgen 'review-report' doc type renders Feedback-shaped review records. Since SecurityFinding IS a Feedback (decision 17's inheritance correction), the renderer already sees the full SecurityFinding object with its extra fields (check ID, evidence, enforcementMode, confidence, override fields, receipt reference) present directly — the renderer's job is simply a type-discriminant check before rendering the dedicated extra-fields section; no rehydration or matching step is needed on the rendering side either. How should the 'review-report' rendering surface those fields for a security review round?
